comments.text:
If Door Dash were to require it, it would not legally be a "tip." It would be an extra charge. (and subject to income taxes) In fact, this would actually be double taxed. (Door Dash would have to pay tax on the money and then the Door Dasher would have to pay taxes on any money that Door Dash forwards to them.)
 
A payment must meet three main requirements to be classified legally as a tip by the IRS:

1. Voluntary: The customer must pay it freely and without compulsion.
2. Unrestricted Amount: The customer must have the sole right to determine the exact amount (or choose to leave the tip line blank).
3. Not Negotiated: The payment cannot be dictated by employer policy or subject to mandatory negotiation.

Mandatory fees or auto-gratuities added to a bill (such as an automatic 18% charge for large parties) are classified as regular service charges or wages, not tips. Even if distributed to staff, service charges are treated as employer gross receipts and standard wage payments.
